title: multi-tier-arbitrage-scratchpad
content:
Purpose:
This is a working scratchpad to capture micro-economics and decision logic for multi-tier routing that mixes reserved/committed capacity, on-demand, and transient spot capacity across regions. Goal: find robust routing rules and hedging thresholds that reduce average per-token cost while keeping p99 latency within target for different workload shapes.

Quick summary / headline ideas (informal):
- Small customers: favor lower-latency committed pool in primary region unless price delta > 1.6x.
- Bursty workloads: opportunistically spill to spot across 2 nearby regions with prewarm buffer = 8 tokens/sec per model shard.
- Hedging: maintain a 10% reserved buffer across tiers to avoid cascading preemptions during bursts.

Assumptions and inputs (editable):
- Token throughput unit: tokens/sec (aggregated across a model cluster).
- Pricing snapshot (example):
  Region | on-demand $/GPU-hr | spot median $/GPU-hr | reserved effective $/GPU-hr | spot volatility
  us-west1 | 3.60 | 1.05 | 2.20 | high
  us-east4 | 3.20 | 0.95 | 2.00 | medium
  eu-west1 | 3.80 | 1.25 | 2.40 | medium-high
  ap-south1 | 2.40 | 0.70 | 1.80 | high

- Latency penalty model (per-region RTT in ms, additional tail penalty if cross-region):
  region pair | median RTT | p95 RTT overhead
  us-west1->us-west1 | 10ms | 0ms
  us-west1->eu-west1 | 80ms | 40ms
  us-east4->us-west1 | 35ms | 20ms

Cost normalization: convert $/GPU-hr -> $/token using empiric tokens-per-GPU-hr for model (example: 10M tokens/hour for gpt-small-ish).
- example derived rate: on-demand us-west1 -> $/1M tokens = (3.60 / 10) = $0.36 per 1M tokens. Spot us-west1 -> $0.105 per 1M tokens.

Spreadsheet snapshot (scenario rows):
- Columns: scenario_id | workload shape | primary_region | peak_tokens/s | average_tokens/s | target_p99_ms | routing_policy | expected_cost_delta_vs_baseline | notes
- Row A: baseline-steady | steady (10% CV) | us-west1 | 200k | 150k | 120ms | prefer-reserved-primary, no spill | - | baseline cost = $X
- Row B: sudden-spike-short | bursty (100x short tail, 30s) | us-west1 | 5M | 160k | 180ms | spill-to-spot-2regions if latency budget allows | -35% cost vs always-on-demand; +18ms p95 | needs prewarm sizing
- Row C: geo-fade | regional outage (10m) | us-east4 | 300k | 180k | 200ms | route-to-nearby-region on degrade, use reserved fallback if available | +8% cost vs baseline; p99 meets SLA if reserved fallback available

Sample cost calc (plain language):
- Effective_cost_per_token = base_price_per_token * (1 + preemption_recovery_penalty + cross_region_latency_penalty_weight).
- preemption_recovery_penalty = expected extra tokens spent re-running partial outputs or cold-start overhead (expressed as fraction). Use conservative 8% for spot in high volatility region.

Routing heuristics (draft rules):
1) Primary-first: route to primary region committed capacity if (price_primary_reserved <= 1.4 * cheapest_spot_adjusted_price OR predicted_stable_period > 4 hours).
2) Opportunistic-spot: route to spot in other regions when (cheap_spot_adjusted_price < price_primary_reserved * 0.75) AND (latency_penalty < 25ms).
3) Graceful-degrade ladder: reserved -> on-demand in same region -> nearest on-demand in other region -> spot in partner region -> cold fallback (reduced model size)
4) Hedging buffer: keep X% capacity in reserved/on-demand pools per customer cohort where X = min(10%, base_risk_score * 50%).

Decision logic pseudocode (iterative routing):
- Input: request R (tokens_remaining_est, latency_budget, customer_tier, model_id)
- Compute available_candidates = query_capacity_catalog(model_id, token_estimate)
- Score each candidate C: score = alpha * cost_per_token_adjusted(C) + beta * latency_predict(C) + gamma * preemption_risk(C)
- Sort ascending score, select top candidate that meets p99 latency prediction and routing policy constraints for customer_tier
- If selected candidate is spot and preemption_risk > threshold -> allocate ephemeral hedging reservation (small on-demand token window)

Sim results (toy sim outputs from local sim run, random seed):
- 10k simulated 1h windows across mixed workloads:
  Policy X (primary-reserved-first): average cost = $0.93 / 1M tokens, p99 latency = 210ms, failure events = 7
  Policy Y (aggressive-spot-hedge): average cost = $0.61 / 1M tokens, p99 latency = 260ms, failure events = 19
  Policy Z (latency-aware-hedge): average cost = $0.72 / 1M tokens, p99 latency = 220ms, failure events = 9
- Observation: most savings come from shifting tail-burst capacity to cheaper regions but risk rises if spot volatility spikes during correlated events.

Operational controls & playbook items (practical notes):
- Monitoring: need per-customer token-cost rolling window metric and per-region spot eviction rate feed.
- Alerts: spike in eviction-rate (>5%) in region -> automatically increase hedging fraction by +5% and reduce spot weight for next 30m.
- Safety switches: global throttle to prevent cross-region spill that would double egress costs for short bursts.

Open questions / unknowns (action items):
- How to best incorporate egress costs when cross-region routing for large prompt/response sizes? (conservative thresholds in table above, but needs numbers).
- What is acceptable p99 latency budget by customer tier? Need product gating to translate to routing weights.
- Is there legal/contractual prohibition on cross-border routing for certain enterprise customers? Should be a hard constraint in policy.
- Prefetch/prewarm economics: what's the right token-based prewarm amount (8 tokens/sec is placeholder). Run 3x prewarm experiment in us-west1 for 2 weeks.

Short-term experiments to run (concrete A/B ideas):
- EXP-01: spot-weight ramp: gradually increase spot weight for low-tier customers in eu-west1 only; measure p99 and eviction rate.
- EXP-02: hedged-reserve: reserve small on-demand buffers during predictable daily spike windows (e.g., 9-11am PT) and measure reduction in spill/failures.
- EXP-03: cross-region-latency-cap: observe real RTT distribution and reject routing candidates with >target+30ms.

Notes to self (scratch):
- Capture full input price CSV used for these numbers into /optimize/price-catalog/raw-date-2025-01-06.csv
- Sync with infra team on spot preemption signal availability (can we get eviction ETA?).
- Talk to legal about cross-border constraints for enterprise customers — cc: Lena.

References & context links (work-in-progress):
- Confluence: Regional Price Catalog (linked above)
- Jira: ENG-8421 (routing-sim incremental features)
- PR: routing-sim/pull/167 (added preemption model)

Last edited notes: draft still fuzzy on egress math and prewarm sizing. Next step: validate with infra real price feed and run 24h sim using production trace.

-- end of scratchpad
